name: Tomas Ibrahim

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am with the independent Work Futures Panel, with no ties to employers, AI firms, unions, parties or government. Your answers stay confidential; what does your factory day involve?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I lead a soft-drinks filling line, from blow-moulder through capper, labeller and shrink-wrap. I keep a notebook of bottles per minute and stop a batch when the labels drift. A two-year technical diploma and years on the line make me one of the strongest operators, but our plant pays below the going rate.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: Who shares the bills, and how do you use new tools?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner Nadia works at a dental reception desk, and our school-age children Yusuf and Hana live with us under a mortgage. Savings would cover less than a month, and there are few similar plants nearby. I use AI now and then to tidy shift reports after another lead has tried a feature; I want a real test before trusting new controls.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: This one is called AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the filling crew that a useful bit of software is fine if it leaves us time to fix crooked labels. The bottling line still needs a person to hear a bad cap before a pallet is filled.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I know that line well and hold a technical diploma, yet our plant pays leads less than the distant brewery. Nadia’s dental reception wage helps, but a mortgage, car loan, two children and less than a month saved leave us exposed if either pay slip is late.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep logging bottles per minute and causes of downtime on my shift. I would keep using the same AI tool now and then to tidy reports, and sit with Nadia to write our household bills on one page; after a full paid month, I would transfer any fresh spare pay into savings.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be anxious about ordinary bills even without dramatic AI. I can tell you the cost of ten idle minutes at work and still hesitate over the car payment at home.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why not take the brewery job?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: It is an hour away, and the travel cost and shift time might erase the advertised raise. I would need a real offer and net pay that covered our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Does a slow month affect the plant?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Head office has talked about moving bottling north before. They have not given us dates, so I keep my notebook instead of treating a rumour as a closure.

say: I would welcome **useful report software** without expecting a revolution.
I would still hear a **bad cap** before bottles reach a pallet.
think: My **lead skill** has not brought the usual wage.
The **mortgage and car loan** are fragile with under one month saved.
do: Keep **filling-line records** and check crooked labels.
Keep using the **existing AI tool** for shift reports.
Write the **household budget** and save fresh full-month surplus.
feel: **Anxious** about existing bills and a very small reserve.

steps.text: Keep logging filling-line output and checking labels
Transfer fresh full-month surplus into household savings

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Now consider Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say ordering software may change the office first, while any camera-driven changeover needs a proper test on our line. The company should show the paid roster before declaring a faster plant.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: One lead could end up covering two lines if the system spots faults and adjusts labels. That might halve my paid hours, and Nadia’s reception wage alone cannot keep the mortgage and children going.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the manager for two written rosters and watch another plant run the new system for a full month. If our plant offers paid supervised practice behind a guard, I would learn the new camera-changeover controls and compare rejects with my notebook; if my hours are cut, I would apply for posted reachable filling jobs only where net pay after travel covers our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be anxious about the possible cut, but I would rather test one changeover than guess. A clean label at four hundred bottles a minute would persuade me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What do you do with an AI report today?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I sometimes use it to tidy my written downtime notes. Learning the new camera controls would be a different task, with a stopped line and a qualified setter beside me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you look at the brewery again?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if it posts a real vacancy with a workable shift. I would subtract the long travel cost before treating its headline pay as better.

I would separate **office planning** from a later physical loader.
think: One lead for two lines could cut **my paid hours**.
Nadia’s **reception wage** cannot carry our family costs alone.
do: Request **two rosters** and observe a month of proven operation.
Learn **new camera controls** only if offered paid guarded practice.
Apply after **hours cuts** for posted reachable filling work with bill-covering pay after travel.
feel: **Anxious** about hours, with a concrete way to test the system.

fieldNote: His **steady technology style** requires a proven run before paid hands-on practice.
Outside work depends on **actual hour cuts**, a posted reachable vacancy and net pay after travel.

steps.text: Request two rosters and observe proven month of changeovers

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Now consider AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the crew that thinking AGI might arrive by 2028 and replace some reception work, while capable hands-on robots reach bottling around 2031. Those are two different dates for our two wages.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect Nadia’s dental reception hours to drop early, then most of my filling-line hours once robots do changeovers. Our reserve is shorter than one month, and I would be awake at night adding up the mortgage and food.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would cancel the planned car replacement and summer trip and write the bills with Nadia this week. If either wage stops, I would apply only for posted reachable work with net pay after travel covering our bills; if no adequate opening appears, I would ask Nadia’s parents whether they can help with school pickup and the lender whether temporary payment terms are possible.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be alarmed by the likely loss of both household wages. My notebook can show a fault, but it cannot make a vacancy appear.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could you sell the car?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only after checking whether we can still reach work and school without it. A sale that costs us a paid shift would leave the mortgage worse off.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you tell the children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell Yusuf and Hana why the trip is off, not make them guess. I would keep their school costs in the budget before another new phone.

say: I would separate **2028 thinking AI** from 2031 bottling robots.
I would ask for **real staffing dates** for both incomes.
think: I expect **reception hours** to fall before filling shifts.
Our **sub-month reserve** cannot bridge two major wage losses.
do: Cancel **car and trip plans** and list the household bills.
Apply after **lost wages** only for posted reachable bill-covering pay after travel work.
Ask **family and lender** for temporary help if no adequate job appears.
feel: **Alarmed** by expected major income loss and sleepless mortgage sums.
S2.quote: My notebook can show a fault, but it cannot make a vacancy appear.
fieldNote: The **reception job** faces thinking AI before physical bottling work does.
Vehicle decisions and employment retain **net-wage conditions**, while lender or family help is not guaranteed.

steps.text: Cancel car and trip plans and list household bills
Apply after wage loss for posted reachable bill-covering pay after travel job

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Now consider AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the plant that thinking AGI in 2031 and capable bottling robots around 2034 give us time for real training places. I want dates and wages on a board, not a promise that everybody will be fine.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At forty-eight I would still need the mortgage wage, and Nadia’s reception work may change earlier. Electrical maintenance might buy us a better route if a local plant is actually hiring at pay we can live on.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep leading the filler and put fresh paid overtime left after bills into savings. If the college offers me a funded electrical-maintenance seat with classes outside paid shifts, Nadia can cover the children, and a posted reachable job has bill-covering net pay, I would enrol; after qualifying, I would apply for that job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be anxious, but five years is enough to check whether the course leads somewhere. I would rather follow a wiring diagram beside a fitter than pay for a seat with no vacancy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who would show you the work safely?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A qualified electrician would isolate a motor and check it is dead before I handle a connection. I would need an actual supervised practical place, not just a classroom seat.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the funded seat does not open?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the paid filler shift and look at posted reachable operator jobs if our own hours are cut. I would not borrow tuition against a mortgage that already feels tight.

say: I would demand **posted training places** before 2034 robots.
I would separate **2031 reception AI** from later filling work.
think: The **mortgage wage** will still matter every month when I reach forty-eight.
A **maintenance ticket** helps only if a reachable plant posts work at adequate net pay.
do: Keep **filler shifts** and save fresh paid overtime after bills.
Enrol in **funded electrical training** only with offered safe practice, classes outside paid shifts, childcare and an adequate posted job.
Apply after **qualification** for that reachable maintenance vacancy.
feel: **Anxious**, with time to verify a real route.
S3.quote: I would rather follow a wiring diagram beside a fitter than pay for a seat with no vacancy.
fieldNote: His **technical confidence** supports electrical learning after an actual funded practical offer.
The **course and application** need a funded safe seat outside paid shifts, childcare, a posted reachable role and bill-covering net wages.

Apply after qualification for posted reachable bill-covering pay after travel maintenance job

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Now consider AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say thinking AGI in 2036 and capable filling robots around 2039 give the plant a decade to post honest training and staffing dates. I would listen to a plan with wages on it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will be fifty-three when thinking systems arrive and fifty-six when robots may do changeovers. Yusuf and Hana will be adults, but I cannot assume the mortgage is gone or that Nadia’s reception hours remain whole.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now in 2026 I would keep the filling line running and transfer any fresh full-month pay left after bills into savings. If I am offered a funded safe practical maintenance place with paid time and a posted reachable job at bill-covering net pay after travel, I would enrol and apply after qualifying; in the first year after 2036, if still employed, I would compare my actual rota with posted local work and apply after a sustained cut only where net pay covers our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be anxious about today’s money, even with ten years ahead. Our next car repair will arrive long before 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you stop working before 2039?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask what our pension and mortgage figures show closer to the time. If we still need my wage and safe work is available, I would keep working.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell the children now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell Yusuf and Hana to compare real paid apprenticeships with their own interests. A job title that sounds safe is no use if nobody nearby is hiring.

say: I would ask for **honest posted dates** and wages.
I would separate **2036 systems** from 2039 physical robots.
think: Our **mortgage and reception hours** may still matter at fifty-six.
A **ten-year warning** does not fix this month’s thin reserve.
do: Keep **2026 filler shifts** and save fresh full-month surplus.
Enrol in **funded paid practical maintenance** only with safe place and adequate posted job.
Apply after **post-2036 cuts** only for posted reachable bill-covering pay after travel work.
feel: **Anxious** about current cash, despite a longer planning window.
S4.quote: Our next car repair will arrive long before 2039.
fieldNote: His **current money pressure** persists despite the distant robot date.
Post-2036 rota checks require **continued employment**; training and work moves require offered safe paid places, local vacancies and adequate net wages.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Which picture worries you most, and what would help?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because reception work could shrink before capable robots reach my filling line around 2031. Written staffing dates, a funded safe practical course and posted reachable work at bill-covering net pay would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I did not ask?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask about the friend across the line. If one lead covers two fillers, somebody has to tell my friend Mo why his name is missing from the rota.

headlineQuote: If one lead covers two fillers, somebody has to tell my friend Mo why his name is missing from the rota.
portrait: **Tomas**, 43, leads a soft-drinks bottling line with a two-year technical diploma and strong practical fault-finding skill.
His **below-market wage**, dental-reception partner, two children, mortgage, sub-month reserve and few nearby plants make job loss serious.
He uses **AI occasionally** for reports and learns new controls after an offered paid safe test on a proven system.
Fast AGI threatens **reception income first**, then hands-on filling work; slower scenarios allow conditional electrical training.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could cut Nadia’s reception hours before capable robots threaten his bottling shifts around 2031.
whatWouldHelp: Written **staffing dates**, offered funded safe maintenance training and posted reachable roles at bill-covering net pay would help.
